screen: Production Google Business after connection (desktop 1440, full page), Stage 5 pass 2

expected_differences: Demo Coffee Co., its business thumbnail, Raleigh address and recorded timestamps replace the Lab’s fictional Loopday identity.
The connected listing exposes six observed issues, including missing fields, two photos and two unanswered reviews. These are legitimate record-dependent states, not missing design content.

Only the phone number and description have concrete proposals with in-app approval. Missing opening hours remain explicit; other changes correctly hand off to Google rather than inventing editable data or approval functionality.
The two review excerpts, 14-review total, 4.6 average and listing facts reflect the production record. The description’s development-data wording does not require an additional demo label.
keep: Mineral canvas, graphite identity/navigation rail, flat white working regions and restrained dividers; no floating app cards or decorative effects.
The 200px rail, 32px desktop content gutter, strong page and section headings, and supporting metadata hierarchy.
Business remains selected, with a visible Settings return path and the existing global navigation.
Observed values under On Google now remain distinct from Proposed values. Each available in-app proposal has its own Approve this change action.
Connected, Missing and Check use literal words alongside color. Read timestamps and Google-reported values provide useful provenance.
Full-size outlined handoff controls, concentrated cobalt approval buttons and ink review links.
The restrained single-column utility layout. This screen needs neither the Lab Content screen’s media assembly nor a decorative source-to-commitment offset.
review.readiness_note: Sign off at the captured 1440px desktop viewport, with one non-blocking copy correction. The capture exposes the expected actions and states; it cannot verify refresh, approval persistence, external navigation or disconnect behavior.

drift.change: Change the section heading from “Fixes you can approve” to “Fix your listing”. Replace its introduction with “Approve available proposals here, one change at a time. Use ‘Change it on Google’ for changes made in your Google Business Profile.” Preserve the existing heading, supporting-text styles and spacing.
drift.why: The current blanket statement, “Nothing changes on Google until you approve it here,” overstates the scope of in-app approval: only two of the six blocks offer Approve, while four correctly hand off to Google. The individual controls are clear, making this a copy correction rather than a functional blocker.
drift.where: Introduction above the opening-hours, phone-number and other listing-fix blocks.

review.why: The supplied Lab image is Content, not a Google Business design, so fidelity is appropriately judged against the shared system. Production preserves the warm neutral surfaces, graphite rail, typography hierarchy, restrained boundaries and meaningful cobalt actions without importing an inappropriate media-heavy composition. Spacing is consistent, controls are comfortably sized, and no text is visibly clipped. The six attention items correspond to six fix blocks; missing observed fields are not filled with proposed values. Review excerpts and listing facts remain accessible below, followed by Open the listing on Google and Disconnect Google. No unrelated money, ranking, search-performance claims or invented connection health appear. Apart from the approval-scope sentence, the screen reads as a faithful, honest management implementation.
review.verdict: Frame Shift was faithfully transferred, and the connected Google Business workflow remains visibly intact, with only a minor approval-scope copy correction.
